# HERPES SIMPLEX ESOPHAGITIS

HSV infection of the esophagus usually occurs in patients who are immunocompromised, typically solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients.
In healthy patients HSV esophagitis occurs occasionally, usually in men under the age of 40.
Patients usually present with odynophagia and dysphagia. Fever, epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and heartburn are less frequent. Some patients may have coexistent herpes labialis or oropharyngeal ulcers. Diagnosis is usually established with an upper endoscopy. Suggestive findings may also be seen during a barium swallow.

## Immunocompetent patients

Spontaneous resolution usually occurs in immunocompetent patients after one to two weeks. Patients may respond more quickly if treated with a short course of oral acyclovir.

## Duration of therapy

Treat for 7-10 days

## Treatment of severe disease

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS
